verdict.rationale: LM Studio runs entirely on the user's own hardware. It also ships llmster, a headless daemon for servers, cloud instances and CI, which can serve models on OpenAI-like endpoints locally and across the network. Community reports confirm the headless flow works with real tools. Community comments about closed source and work-use license limits concern openness rather than the ability to self-host, so they lower quality but are not a dispute. Missing for 10: source availability or open-source code, detailed server deployment documentation (e.g. containers or install guides), and a license permitting work use of the self-hosted install.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: llmster is the headless version of LM Studio, no desktop app required. It's ideal for servers, CI environments, or any machine where you don't need a GUI.
llmster is LM Studio's headless daemon for servers, cloud instances, and CI.
Serve local models on OpenAI-like endpoints, locally and on the network
The headless LM Studio flow is especially nice because it makes local inference usable from real tools instead of as a demo.
